items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: Such as Lee Collins, uh, John Marrero, Simon Marrero

ctx.x: Who is at the La Vida with you? You were talking about that.

Oh, I mentioned the fellow that was at the La Vida with me already. Such as Lee Collins, uh, John Marrero, Simon Marrero, uh, Roy Evans was there with me on drums, and Alfred William on drums, and, uh, David Jones on tennis sax, Rubichaud on piano.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: And I think Simon played big, John played with him too.

ctx.x: Well, that would have been Joe Watson in those times. Yeah, yeah. Who was a Yanker buddy, I could never remember. Yanker. Yanker. And Alfred on drums. I guess Marrero on bass, Simon Drunk. I don't know, I forget it.

And I think Simon played big, John played with him too. John played with him too. Yeah, John played with him too. Yeah, John played with him. And Simon. Yeah. And, yeah, I wasn't with him then. Isaiah wasn't with him then. That was his earlier band. But after Isaiah started playing underneath, he worked out there in his band as the second trumpet player. Yeah.

Well they didn't have anything particular. I just liked a lot of ragtime stuff, jump stuff. I didn't like nothing too slow. Bless me was the blues. Now if you could play the blues for them all night they didn't like that. Just nothing but the blues but nothing slow like stardust or something like that. They didn't like nothing like that. That was too slow they didn't want that. But if you play the blues in that temple right down the alley they liked that. They used to uh get off from work around. And they did a…
Is that Simon or Eddie Marrero on which one? Simon. Simon was on bass.

And drums? Drummer was Alfred William. And yourself, what were you playing then? I was playing clarinet. Still? No, I was playing saxophone then. Yeah, because I started fooling with saxophone when I was at the hummingbird.
